solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A celeb — and what a physique!

definitions.meaning: a celebrity is a person of note, a big name
an exclamation admiring a fine figure, read as two words

explanation.surface: An admiring remark about a famous person who also happens to look good.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is someone who matters, a name people know; split in two, the word also praises an impressive frame.

clue.text: Having me get hold of a horse to run

indicators.note: one word gets hold of, encloses, the other

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Someone told to grab a horse and race it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to be in charge of it, to control it.

clue.text: One of the rules of cricket?

definitions.text: One of the rules of cricket?

parts.words: One of the rules of cricket?
parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched

explanation.definitionFit: A local regulation made by a council, playfully read as a law about the cricket extra called a bye.

clue.text: Prevent profit from one being late

definitions.text: Prevent profit from one being late

parts.words: Prevent profit from one being late
parts.note: 'the late' means the dead; stopping someone gaining from a dead person's estate is cutting them out of the will

explanation.definitionFit: To cut an heir out of a will, so they gain nothing from a dead relative's estate.

clue.text: Pleased with the sundial

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for sun, as on weather charts and calendars (Sunday)
dial is slang for the face, as is mug

explanation.surface: Someone delighted with the garden sundial they have just installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sundial' must be split: 'sun' gives S and 'dial', slang for the face, gives MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied, complacently content with oneself, which is a sense of being pleased.

clue.text: Shoo the mule wandering about vineyard plant

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, enclosing it
the word mule wanders, its letters straying into a new order

parts.note: scat and shoo are both cries to drive an animal off

explanation.surface: Driving off a mule that is roaming round a vineyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoo' looks like an order to the mule, but it is a synonym; 'wandering' scrambles the mule to MUEL, which goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscat grape variety grown on vines for sweet wine, so a plant of the vineyard.

clue.text: Denied I sang out "Help!"

indicators.note: the letters come out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer protesting that they never cried out for help.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb for contradicted or opposed, so a synonym for denied.

clue.text: Having returned, were in the sand playing

indicators.note: one word goes in the other, a container signal
the word sand is played with, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Children back from the beach, having played in the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads as came back but means replied; 'playing' gives ANSD around which nothing goes: the other piece sits 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a remark is to reply, so replied is the sense here.

clue.text: Shrink and send off, once freshly wrapped

indicators.note: one set of letters is wrapped round the other, so it is a container signal
the word once is made fresh, its letters set out in a new order
the word send goes off, its letters scrambled into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to compress a document and post it, newly packaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send off' reads as posting, but 'off' scrambles the first word (to DENS) and 'freshly' the other (to CONE); 'wrapped' puts one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress or reduce in size or volume is to make smaller, a direct synonym.

clue.text: With a gentle rebuke, taking care of myself

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: Someone gently scolded while looking after themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as 'come, come!' or 'come now', it is a mild reproof.

clue.text: Unexpectedly sees good in spots

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so it marks a container
the word sees arrives in an unexpected order, scrambled

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is a crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A surprised observer notices something good in a patch of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like blemishes but is the verb for notices; 'Unexpectedly' scrambles the other verb to ESES around the good letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or notice something is a verb synonym, as in 'she spots a ship'.

clue.text: I'm changing gear in another way. It's a pain

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order, so this signals rearrangement
set out another way means arranged differently, a second rearrangement signal

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A driver grinding the gearbox who finds the whole business a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' and 'another way' both point to rearranging the letters of I'M, GEAR and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe recurring headache, which is a kind of pain.

clue.text: Misinform about the animal — a dog

indicators.note: one word goes about, round, the other, signalling a container

parts.note: the ass is the animal meant, the donkey

explanation.surface: Someone giving false information about which creature is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous fictional collie from film and television, so a dog by name.

clue.text: He's back on the line with new offer (change of heart)

indicators.note: the word offer is made new, its letters rearranged
a change of heart here rearranges the letters of the word heart

explanation.surface: A man back on the telephone with a fresh bid, having changed his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OFFER into FOREF and 'change of' rearranges HEART into ATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone further back in the family line, so earlier in the lineage.

clue.text: Early, while the pub is still open

definitions.meaning: ahead of the due hour, sooner than expected

definitions.text: while the pub is still open
definitions.meaning: before closing time is called in a British pub

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb for formerly or in advance, and literally before 'time', the pub landlord's closing call.

clue.text: Challenges in courts, set on overthrowing

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, a container signal

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court, so CTS for courts

indicators.note: the words set on are overthrown, their letters tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Legal challenges in court, aimed at toppling something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenges in courts' tempts as a long definition, but 'in' is the container; 'overthrowing' scrambles the two short words into ONTES.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or oppose something, such as a will or a seat, is to challenge it.

clue.text: Gave it one's all, though injured

definitions.meaning: made every effort, tried as hard as possible
hurt, as a pulled muscle is

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both exerting oneself to the limit and a muscle that has been pulled or hurt.

clue.text: Not drinking from the little cup at all

definitions.text: Not drinking from the little cup at all

parts.words: Not drinking from the little cup at all
parts.note: the little cup is the cup that holds alcohol; someone who never takes a drop abstains completely

explanation.definitionFit: Totally abstaining from alcohol, never touching a drop of strong drink.

clue.text: Prepared then to concoct lies, making whoopee

indicators.note: the words then and to are prepared, worked into a new order
to concoct is to cook up, so the word lies is mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone ready to fabricate a story while living it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges THEN TO into ONTHET and 'concoct' rearranges LIES into ILES.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for a night of wild revelry, which is making whoopee in American slang.

clue.text: Shooters hose off swarming horseflies

indicators.note: the letters of hose come off the larger word
what remains swarms about into a new order

explanation.surface: Using a garden hose to drive away a swarm of horseflies.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H, O, S, E from HORSEFLIES leaves RFLIES, which 'swarming' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms with grooved barrels, guns being shooters in informal speech.

clue.text: Caution about entering the tunnel

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, a container signal

explanation.surface: A safety warning about going into a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A network of rabbit burrows, an underground maze of passages dug by animals.

clue.text: He has a drink once one leaves

indicators.note: one word leaves the other, a deletion signal

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A man who has a drink now and then once a companion has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes the letters ONE out of ONCE, leaving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so a male person, referred to as he.

clue.text: It's included among potential star qualities

indicators.note: one piece is put among the letters of the other, a container signal
the word star is only potential, its letters still to be arranged

parts.note: the word it, with 's read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A talent scout noting the qualities that mark someone out as a future star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges STAR into TRAS, and IT goes among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics or distinguishing features of a person, a synonym for qualities.

clue.text: Great number to finish off with

parts.note: capital is an old-fashioned word for excellent or great
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A large figure arrives as the closing touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to top everything, to round things off as a final blow or flourish.

clue.text: Speak about an idiot with good sense

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a fool who nonetheless shows good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind and reasonable judgement, the condition of being sensible.

clue.text: Angry when a small quantity of her oil dripped in

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, a container signal

parts.note: a cc, cubic centimetre, is a small quantity of liquid

indicators.note: the letters of her and oil are dripped out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Someone cross because a tiny drop of her oil was let in.
explanation.walkthrough: A cc is a cubic centimetre; 'dripped' scrambles the pronoun and the liquid into HOLERI, which goes 'in' that small measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-tempered and irritable, from the old humour of yellow bile; a synonym for irate.

clue.text: Pointless if it's cloudy

definitions.meaning: without an edge or interest, blunt or boring

explanation.definitionFit: Both a blunt or tedious thing and an overcast sky can be described with this one adjective.

clue.text: Furnishes with items one hasn't paid for

definitions.meaning: to give or supply someone with something

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means gives or supplies; as a plural noun it means gifts received for nothing.
